gloss: to stock, to purchase for resale

definitions.gloss: to stock, to purchase (goods for resale), to procure
definitions.explanation: To buy goods from a supplier or wholesaler for the purpose of selling them to customers. A fundamental business term in retail and commerce.

examples.japanese: {新鮮|しんせん}な{野菜|やさい}を{仕入|しい}れる。
examples.english: To stock up on fresh vegetables.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{市場|いちば}で{魚|さかな}を{仕入|しい}れている。
examples.english: Every morning I purchase fish at the market.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}から{安|やす}く{仕入|しい}れた{商品|しょうひん}をネットで{販売|はんばい}している。
examples.english: I sell products online that I purchased cheaply from overseas.

notes:
CONJUGATION: {仕入|しい}れる is an ichidan verb. Te-form: {仕入|しい}れて. Noun form: {仕入|しい}れ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {商品|しょうひん}を{仕入|しい}れる (to purchase goods)
- {仕入|しい}れ{値|ね} (purchase price, cost price)
- {仕入|しい}れ{先|さき} (supplier, vendor)

FIGURATIVE: Can also be used figuratively to mean acquiring information or knowledge: {情報|じょうほう}を{仕入|しい}れる (to gather information).
